eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket heavily favors highs of 62-65°F for San Francisco on May 3, with 62-63°F leading at 43% implied probability, reflecting the latest National Weather Service guidance projecting a high near 65°F amid persistent marine layer influence. Cool marine air advection from west-southwest winds around 6-10 mph, typical of the "May Gray" stratus deck, is capping temperatures via a shallow temperature inversion, as seen in recent overnight lows near 53-54°F on May 2. Model ensembles from NOAA's GFS and ECMWF show a tight 62-66°F spread, with coastal fog burn-off timing as the key uncertainty; historical May 3 averages hover at 65°F at SFO station, but recent cool biases in observations have nudged odds cooler. Watch for afternoon NWS updates refining peak heating potential.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from ECMWF, GFS, and Russia's Hydrometeorological Center show a consensus daytime high near 18–21°C for Moscow on May 3, driving the tight clustering of trader odds at 29% for 21°C, 26% for 19°C, and 25.5% for 20°C. Differentiating factors include model discrepancies on afternoon cloud cover—potentially capping peaks at 19°C (YR.no, AccuWeather) or allowing 21–23°C under sunnier conditions (Gismeteo, Ventusky)—plus station-specific measurements at Vnukovo or similar sites. New 12Z model runs and intraday observations could refine this uncertainty before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in Cape Town's May 3 highest temperature at Cape Town International Airport, with 22°C (31%) and 23°C (30.5%) edging out 21°C (20.5%) amid the South African Weather Service's (SAWS) latest forecast of a 21°C maximum under fine to partly cloudy skies and light southerlies. May climatology averages 20°C highs, with resolution hinging on observed cloud cover and wind timing; SAWS updates at 05:00 and 16:00 SAST today may shift odds further.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket closely splits between 27°C (34%) and 28°C (34%) for Guangzhou's highest temperature on May 3, reflecting official China Meteorological Administration forecasts projecting a daytime peak of 27°C amid heavy rain and widespread cloud cover that will suppress solar heating. Ensemble models like GFS and ECMWF exhibit minimal spread around 27.5°C, with 26°C (19%) viable if showers intensify midday; 29°C+ odds remain low absent clearing. Overnight forecast updates from CMA and international agencies could refine this narrow range before resolution.
